chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Ali ibn Hadid, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the testimony of women in marriage without a man with them, when the woman is in dispute, and he said, 'There is no objection to it.'
Then he said to me, 'What do your jurists say about that?' I said, 'They say that the testimony of two just men is not permissible [as sufficient].'
He said, 'They lied; may Allah curse them. They lightened and trivialized the binding commands and obligations of Allah, and they strengthened and magnified what Allah lightened.'
Indeed, Allah commanded in divorce the testimony of two just men, yet they validated divorce with only one witness.

And marriage did not come from Allah with a prohibition [requiring witnesses] in its essence, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) established the two witnesses as a discipline and consideration so that the child and inheritance would not be disputed.
And the marriage contract is established and the private part becomes permissible, even if no witness is present.
And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) validated the testimony of two women in marriage in case of dispute, and he did not validate in divorce except the testimony of two just men.
I said, 'Then how [do you explain] the mention of Allah, Exalted is He, and His saying, 'A man and two women'?

He said, 'That is in debt, when there are not two men, [then] a man and two women, and one man, and the oath of the claimant when there are not two women. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) after him judged by that among you.'

As for what the report included that their testimony is not accepted in the fixed punishments, it is to be understood as referring to when they are alone without men, as we clarified in what preceded.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on the validity of two women's testimony for marriage contracts?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the jurists for inappropriately applying the divine strictness of divorce to marriage, arguing that the requirement for two men in divorce is a specific command, whereas marriage witnesses are a prophetic precaution (tadib) to preserve lineage. He clarifies that the Quranic 'man and two women' verse (2:282) pertains to financial debts, not marital contracts, and notes that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) also accepted two women's testimony in disputed marriages. This hadith highlights the Shia distinction between divine obligations and prophetic disciplinary measures in legal jurisprudence.
